summary: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an offline, GPU-accelerated desktop Geographical Information System (GIS) designed to solve critical surface navigation challenges for astronauts and pressurized rovers in Jezero Crater, Mars. Unlike conventional routing tools that only minimize distance, this platform uses a custom multi-criteria A-star pathfinding engine to optimize six life-critical constraints across a 400x400 digital elevation model: safe slope limits (15 degrees or less) to prevent rollover, ionizing radiation exposure, extreme day-night temperature stress, aeolian sand traps, proximity to natural rock shelters, and real-time energy (kWh) and oxygen consumption. Built with Python, PyQt6, and OpenGL using authentic NASA datasets (MOLA, THEMIS, MEDA, and RAD), it delivers interactive 2D and 3D terrain visualization, engineering trade-off reports, and exportable mission telemetry.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is a standalone, GPU-accelerated desktop Geographical Information System (GIS) engineered for extravehicular activity (EVA) astronauts and pressurized rovers operating in Jezero Crater, Mars. Built upon a 400x400 Digital Elevation Model (DEM) derived from Jezero Crater topography (jezero.stl), the application deploys a custom multi-criteria A-star pathfinding engine. Rather than calculating only the shortest geometric distance, the software simultaneously computes and compares three distinct traverse strategies—the Optimal Survival Route, the Shortest Geometric Route, and the Minimum-Slope Route—across interactive 2D tactical maps and 3D perspective terrain views.

Factors Considered & Innovation

Unlike terrestrial navigation tools, planetary exploration requires balancing competing survival hazards. Our team designed a multi-layered analytical pipeline that evaluates six critical constraints across every grid cell:

1. Traversable Slope Limits: Enforces safe inclination margins (defaulting to 15 degrees or less) to prevent rover rollover and crew slip hazards on steep crater scarps.

2. Ionizing Radiation Exposure: Evaluates Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) and Solar Particle Event dose rates using topographic shielding.

3. Diurnal Thermal Stress: Models extreme daytime and nighttime surface temperature swings to account for battery discharge and heater loads.

4. Aeolian Sand-Trap Mitigation: Identifies low-inertia regolith and loose sand formations to prevent wheel embedment and immobilization.

5. Natural Shelter & Science Access: Maps six natural bedrock shelters (SHL-01 to SHL-06) for emergency protection alongside eight astrobiology sample stations (SMP-01 to SMP-08).

6. Consumables & Reserve Margins: Tracks real-time energy expenditure (kWh) and oxygen consumption (liters) against configurable emergency reserve thresholds.

Benefits & Intended Impact

The platform empowers mission planners and field crews to make data-driven routing decisions that maximize human safety and mission longevity. By visualizing hidden environmental hazards in advance, Martian Map prevents life-threatening situations such as rover entrapment in sand dunes or excessive radiation exposure, while conserving critical battery and life-support reserves. Furthermore, the system automatically generates an Engineering Route Justification Report explaining why riskier alternatives were rejected, and exports mission briefings in JSON and CSV formats for offline field execution without requiring internet connectivity.

Tools, Programming Languages & Data Sources

- Programming Language & Core Libraries: Developed in Python 3 using NumPy for vectorized matrix operations and SciPy for spatial distance transforms.

- Graphics & User Interface: Built with PyQt6 and PyOpenGL to deliver smooth 2D/3D terrain visualization, real-time cursor telemetry, and dynamic elevation/slope profile charts.

- Deployment: Packaged via PyInstaller into a self-contained Windows executable for zero-dependency offline use.

- NASA Planetary Datasets: Environmental simulation layers and terrain models are grounded in data from MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter), MRO/HiRISE, Mars Odyssey THEMIS, Mars 2020 Perseverance MEDA, and MSL RAD.
